chunks: I asked him about the woman who menstruates and then the time of her purity passes while she still sees blood. So he said: She should wait cautiously for one day, if her menstruation is less than ten days. If the blood continues, then she is a mustahadha (woman with istihaaza). If the blood stops, she should perform ghusl and pray. He said: I said to him, 'What about the woman whose menstruation is seven or eight days, her cycle being constant and regular, then she menstruates for three days, then the blood stops and she sees whiteness — neither yellowness nor blood?' He said: 'She should perform ghusl and pray.' I said, 'She performs ghusl, prays, and fasts, then the blood returns?' He said: 'When she sees blood, she should withhold from salat and fasting.' I said, 'What if she sees blood one day and is pure the next day?' He said: 'When she sees blood, she should withhold; when she sees purity, she should pray. When the days of her menstruation have passed and purity continues with her, she should pray. Then if she sees blood, she is a mustahadha. I have laid out all of her matters for you completely.'

key_terms.اسْتِحَاضَة: Istihaaza — irregular/inter-period bleeding that is not haydh; worship is permitted after ghusl
key_terms.تَسْتَظْهِر: To observe cautiously; waiting an extra day before concluding menstruation has ended
key_terms.حَيْض: Haydh — menstruation; the state of ritual impurity that suspends salat and fasting
key_terms.طُهْر: Tuhr — the state of ritual purity between menstrual cycles

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Shia Islam for a woman whose menstrual blood continues past the expected purity time?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a comprehensive jurisprudential dialogue between a questioner and Imam al-Sadiq (AS) on distinguishing regular menstruation (haydh) from irregular bleeding (istihaaza). The Imam provides detailed rulings for three scenarios: a woman still seeing blood after her expected purity period, a woman with a stable cycle that temporarily shortens, and a woman alternating between blood and purity day by day. The key principle is that haydh suspends salat and fasting, while istihaaza permits worship after ghusl. The Imam concludes with the authoritative statement that these rulings collectively resolve all such situations, reflecting the Shia tradition of deriving detailed fiqh directly from the infallible Imams.
